sentences.text: Sharks are older than trees. Not by a little, by tens of millions of years. So how is that possible?
The earliest shark-like scales show up in fossils about 450 million years old.
The first true trees appear around 385 million years ago, and dinosaurs only about 245 million years back.
That means shark ancestors were already swimming for over 60 million years before the first forest grew.
Since then, sharks have survived all five mass extinctions, including the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs.
Their skeleton is cartilage, not bone, which is why most shark fossils are just teeth.
One catch: modern shark species are younger than trees. So are sharks living fossils, or the ocean's oldest family business? Tell me in the comments.
